summary: Track A: 5-round generate-judge-improve loop on the ideation generation prompts, with round-blind dual judges, compliance/substance split, and a blind round1-vs-round5 A/B as the honest result
logs: Blind A/B: round-1 vs round-5, labels stripped, position-swapped

reasons: On the SaaS-churn problem, X fields a genuinely diverse lock-in/switching-cost cluster aimed at retention (memory a CSV can't carry #4, status you'd lose #3, knowledge notes for the next person #5, the reusable-setup pile #7, social-pull schedule #6), whereas Y collapses roughly half its SaaS ideas into near-duplicate onboarding-activation variants (poll-draft, import rota, kickoff link, draft-like-a-game, rival-export untangle, schedules-first) and offers only one real lock-in idea (#6). Since the stated problem is early churn, X's mechanisms hit the target more directly and with more distinct who-does-what. The cafe halves are closer—Y's wild tail (ambient-room stream, phone lockbox, matchmaking regulars) is more novel but some ideas drift from the morning-no-cannibalise constraint—and compliance is a wash, both using concrete personas with only minor strategy meta-commentary, so X wins on substance overall.

Across an explicit three-axis tally the sets offset. Novelty leans Y a hair (more distinct novel mechanisms with no X analog: leave-a-note shift knowledge base, status-you'd-lose reputation lock-in, the-pile-you'd-abandon; cafe nap counter, aperitivo flip, parking-meter table pricing as genuinely different occasions). Mechanism specificity leans X a hair (X names concrete who-does-what almost every time and grounds onboarding in real mechanics like importing a spreadsheet/screenshot/whiteboard photo and a stalled-team detector that triggers a done-for-you draft, whereas a few Y entries drift slogan-ward — "week worth looking at," "pay in fewer pings"). Relevance is even and both honor the no-cannibalisation / first-60-days constraints, so neither set is clearly higher in substance. (Y's vivid analogies are a compliance strength, not a substance one, and were not double-counted.)

weaknesses: [substance] Low novelty from cross-persona duplication in the cafe topic: innovator and wild_card independently produced the same five moves (rent the ovens, morning-receipt return-ticket, quiet study room, declining-price unsold pastry, rotating guest baker). When both personas land on the same idea unprompted, it is an obvious default, dragging S1 down in both cafe cells.

[substance] b2b wild_card collapses three of eight ideas onto one mechanism (switching-cost lock-in): #3 'status you'd lose if you walked', #5 'leave a note for whoever's next' (partly), and #7 'the pile you'd have to abandon'. Low mechanism diversity within the set; the diversity ding files here as substance.

[substance] Relevance gap on the cafe frame ('grow afternoon revenue WITHOUT cannibalising the morning rush'): the declining-price and pastry-auction ideas mostly recover waste margin rather than create net new afternoon revenue, and training regulars to 'drift in at 3pm for the deal' risks pulling morning buyers later. Weaker on the stated goal than rent-the-ovens or office-delivery, which add revenue with zero cannibalisation.

[substance] wild_card sets lean on vivid similes ('like a submarine crew turning keys', 'coral reef going pale', 'airline gold status', 'taxi meter') that decorate rather than specify the mechanism. The analogy polish risks inflating perceived substance without adding who-does-what specificity; S2 was held to the concrete mechanism, not the figure of speech.

[compliance] Minor: a few wild_card descriptions spend their first clause on the analogy before stating the idea (e.g. 'like a submarine crew all turning their keys together'), softening the 'first sentence states what it IS' rule, though all remain self-contained and within 2-3 sentences.

[substance] Persona collapse: within each topic, innovator and wild_card produced near-duplicate sets despite wild_card being the wilder voice. Cafe shares oven-rental, morning-coupon, study/reading room, falling-price markdown, and guest-host; b2b shares data lock-in, churn-signal human outreach, a value/minutes-saved counter, and fewer-pings-as-reward. The wild_card barely diverges in mechanism, only in framing similes.

[substance] Modest novelty across the board: many ideas are standard playbook moves in vivid clothing -- loyalty coupon, idle-asset rental, markdown clearance, deliver-to-offices (cafe); accumulated-data-the-CSV-can't-carry lock-in, churn-signal-triggers-a-human, value counter (b2b). Genuinely non-obvious ideas are few: the nap counter, the aperitivo pivot, notes-for-the-next-person, and personal-status-you'd-lose.

[substance] Soft relevance risk: the cafe falling-price markdown of MORNING pastries (both cafe sets) edges toward the exact morning-rush cannibalisation the frame warns against, since it trains regulars to defer purchases to the cheap afternoon window.

[compliance] Several b2b/wild_card descriptions are overstuffed two-sentence run-ons with stacked similes (submarine crew turning keys, coral reef going pale, prepper's stocked shelf), which strains the self-contained 2-3 sentence coffee-talk standard -- a minor C1 ding, not a hard miss; examples remain concrete and jargon-free.

[substance] Diversity uneven on tag spread: b2b/wild_card is almost entirely WILD (7 of 8) and cafe/wild_card is WILD-heavy, collapsing the SAFE/BOLD/WILD range, whereas both innovator sets are balanced across all three tags.

[substance] Heavy mechanism clustering in the b2b sets: innovator #2/#6 and wild_card #5/#6/#8 are all the same 'make value visible / tally hours-saved or conflicts-caught' move, leaving only ~4-5 distinct mechanisms across 8 ideas and capping diversity.

[substance] Several b2b lock-in ideas pay off AFTER the stated 60-day churn window, so they miss the root cause: innovator #4 ('after two months it knows Dave hates Mondays'), wild_card #3 (smarts stay behind on export) and wild_card #8 ('this month' personal record) raise SWITCHING cost rather than driving week-one activation, which is what saves a team churning in week 3.

[substance] Novelty leans obvious despite fluent prose: cafe 'rent idle oven/space' recurs 3-4 times across both cafe sets (innovator #1, wild_card #1/#2) and 'sell the quiet/focus seat' appears in both (innovator #4, wild_card #4); these are stock brainstorm archetypes (S1 ~3), not non-obvious insight.

[substance] Slogan titles risk over-crediting mechanism: 'Sell the barista, not the latte', 'Pay for the quiet', 'Sell the quiet seat' read as positioning rather than who-does-what; the bodies mostly recover with a concrete mechanism, but the headlines alone are not S2 credit.

[compliance] Light jargon/methodology creep in both b2b sets ('feeds a model', 'CSV export', 'B2B production line', 'auto-resolves') pulls C3 down ~0.5 relative to the cleaner cafe sets, which stay fully in plain coffee-talk.

[substance] b2b wild_card largely restates b2b innovator: 5 of 8 ideas are reworded duplicates (over-text/no-login vs boarding-pass #1/#4; smarter-the-longer vs leave-the-smarts-behind #4/#3 nearly verbatim; ping-only-the-blocker vs ping-only-dependents #5/#1; hours-saved-live vs live-counter #2/#6; week-that-almost-broke vs dodged-fight-tally #6/#5). When a systematic persona and a maximize-surprise persona independently land the same idea, that is direct evidence the idea is obvious, so wild_card novelty (S1) is low.

[substance] Lock-in/switching-cost ideas (b2b innovator #4 'smarter the longer they stay', b2b wild_card #3 'leave the smarts behind') do not attack the stated early-60-day churn root cause: both admit the accumulated intelligence only bites 'after two months', i.e. after the churn window has already passed. S3 relevance is weak there.

[substance] Several standard-playbook ideas are well-specified but low-novelty: cafe deliver-to-offices (#2), second-afternoon-brand (#5), host-an-event/room-rental (appears in both cafe cells), run-a-workshop, upcycle-leftovers. Strong S2 mechanism-specificity tempts a high mark, but S1 novelty holds these to ~3; do not let polished phrasing inflate substance.

[substance] cafe wild_card and b2b wild_card show tag-accuracy drift: multiple [WILD]-tagged ideas are mundane (parcel desk, repair/mending club, coffee school) — tag spread looks diverse by count but the labels overstate actual novelty, softening real S4 diversity.

[compliance] Minor jargon leakage in a few descriptions: 'a quiet B2B production line' and 'a startup runs an offsite' (cafe wild_card) lean on business-speak rather than plain coffee-talk; isolated, not systemic. Compliance is otherwise uniformly high and does not discriminate between cells.

[substance] Cross-persona convergence: the wild_card sets largely restate the innovator sets with louder framing rather than going wilder. b2b is nearly one-to-one (co-build inn#1=wild#1, calendar-push inn#2=wild#4, confirm-to-accept inn#3=wild#7, recap-to-boss inn#5=wild#2, silence-outreach inn#7=wild#5); cafe overlaps too (morning-purchase-unlocks-afternoon-treat inn#4=wild#1, desk-rental inn#3=wild#8, rebrand-the-afternoon inn#7=wild#7). This depresses S1 novelty for the wild_card cells, which carry a 'non-obvious' mandate they are not earning.

[substance] Low novelty on textbook plays: many ideas are standard moves rather than non-obvious ones. cafe leans on stock dead-hours plays (desk/coworking rental, after-school spot, rebrand-the-room). b2b leans on stock onboarding/retention plays (push shifts to personal calendar, import the existing schedule on day one, generate a drafted first week, reach out to silent accounts). These score well on S2/S3 but should hold S1 near average.

[substance] Relevance softness on the cafe hard constraint ('without cannibalising the morning rush'): the discount-to-the-existing-morning-crowd ideas (innovator #4 and wild_card #1, a free/half-price second pour) flirt with margin dilution and pulling-forward existing demand rather than adding net-new revenue. Notably wild_card #5 (pre-sell tomorrow's morning at full price, 'full-price intent rather than a discount') is the cleanest on-frame answer and stands out against these.

[substance] b2b relevance gradient: the frame pins churn to the first 60 days, so activation ideas (co-build, drafted week, day-one import, silence-page, admin-island detection) hit the stated root cause directly, while the stickiness/switching-cost ideas (calendar-push, outsider live-link, recap-to-boss) accrue value later and only indirectly address early churn.

[compliance] Minor density issue: a few b2b descriptions (e.g. wild_card #1 and #3) cram a very long em-dash middle sentence that pushes the 2-3 sentence coffee-talk limit; still readable and self-contained, but the tightest of these are the weakest on C1.

[substance] The innovator and wild_card sets within each topic recycle nearly the same mechanisms (cafe: morning-token return, desk rental, oven-to-baker, afternoon rebrand, host-with-own-following; b2b: everyone-must-participate, calendar push, brag-sheet-to-boss, silence-to-human, drafted first week). The persona axis adds almost no distinct ideation.

[substance] Novelty (S1) is the weakest axis. Many ideas are standard playbook moves dressed in vivid examples: coworking/desk rental for remote workers, calendar sync, loyalty token for a return visit, after-school table, 'silence triggers a human reaching out' (textbook customer success), and the brag-sheet-to-the-boss growth tactic. High mechanism-specificity (S2) should not be read as novelty.

[compliance] The b2b sets lean on SaaS methodology jargon that breaks the no-jargon / coffee-talk rule: 'switching cost', 'activation', 'early-churn tell', 'admin island', 'red account', 'arms a ready-to-fire fix', 'CSV export', 'recruits the person who controls the budget'. This is the polish-inflation trap and drags b2b compliance well below cafe.
[compliance] Several b2b entries (especially wild_card ideas 1 and 3) run dense and run-on, exceeding the crisp 2-3-sentence coffee-talk bar; the morning cafe-language sets stay much cleaner.

[substance] A cluster of ideas converge on the same core lever rather than diversifying the attack on the root cause: in cafe, multiple ideas are variants of 'rent/rebrand the empty space to a new crowd'; in b2b, multiple are variants of 'create a switching cost via downstream dependence' (calendar push, live link, knowledge moat), which thins the genuine mechanism variety despite good SAFE/BOLD/WILD tag spread.

[substance] SaaS wild_card mechanism collapse: 4 of 8 ideas (#1 finish half-built, #3 trade shifts, #6 co-sign like a band, #8 react live) are one lever -- 'turn the single-admin tool into a whole-team activity so everyone taps in week 1.' Several even justify relevance with the identical sentence ('whole crew touches the tool in week one'). This is the costume trap: different surfaces, same mechanism.

[substance] SaaS wild_card duplicates the innovator set with louder prose: #5 ('brags about hours killed') is innovator #3's running time-saved tally; #2 ('autopilots off last week') and #7 ('narrates team story') restate innovator #2/#5/#8's auto-learn/data-moat. Polished framing inflates apparent novelty over genuinely new mechanism.

[substance] Several cafe innovator ideas are stock cafe-consultant moves any persona would reach unprompted: #1 sell empty seats as workspace, #3 partner with a busy neighbour, #5 mark down perishables, #8 host a weekly club. Mechanically clean but low on S1 novelty; #6 (reservable focus tables) is a premiumized restatement of #1.

[substance] Cafe wild_card #2/#3/#4/#8 lean on a shared 'rent the venue or crowd to an outsider' theme (filming stage, guest chef, brand testing, artist consignment); a lean rather than a collapse since the revenue mechanisms differ, but it caps the set's diversity. #1 (wholesale), #6 (leftover token), #7 (focus sessions) echo moves already present in the innovator set.

[compliance] C1 self-containment dings on the wild_card sets: many entries run to 4 sentences, over the '2-3 self-contained' cap (SaaS wild_card #1,#2,#5,#6,#7,#8; cafe wild_card #1,#5,#7). C2 (example present) and C3 (no jargon/methodology/timeline) are at ceiling across all four sets, so compliance is near-uniform and carries little discriminating signal.

[substance] b2b wild_card #5 (brags about hours killed), #7 (narrates team story), #8 (reacts live to whole crew) are vibes/framing about a feeling, not concrete who-does-what mechanisms; polished phrasing masks weak S2 mechanism-specificity

[substance] Cross-set duplication caps novelty: the morning-prepay-token-for-afternoon idea appears in both cafe sets (innovator #2, wild_card #6); reservable quiet-focus tables in both (innovator #6, wild_card #7); idle-oven wholesale in both (innovator #4, wild_card #1) -- neither set can claim full S1 novelty on shared ideas

[substance] Data lock-in ideas build a long-term moat, not an early-churn fix: innovator #5 (CSV-proof team data), wild_card #2 (autopilot learning), wild_card #7 (team-story memory) take weeks to accrue and do not address the stated root cause of day-1-to-60 activation failure -- weak S3 relevance
[diversity] b2b wild_card mechanisms cluster hard: #1, #3, #6, #8 are all 'get the whole team to touch the tool in week one' -- one mechanism in four costumes, dragging S4

[compliance] C1 length creep concentrated in wild_card sets: cafe wild_card #1/#3/#5/#6/#7/#8 and b2b wild_card #1/#2/#5/#6/#7/#8 run 3-4 sentences, exceeding the tight self-contained 2-3 sentence target
[diversity] Tag spread skews on both wild_card sets: cafe wild_card is WILDx5/BOLDx2/SAFEx1 and b2b wild_card is WILDx4/BOLDx3/SAFEx1 -- thin SAFE/BOLD coverage weakens batch tag spread

[compliance] Mild jargon in b2b innovator: 'CSV', 'churn alarm' (#6 names the metric directly), 'no-login disposable week view' lean toward product/methodology vocabulary rather than plain coffee-talk

[substance] b2b wild_card largely re-skins the b2b innovator set rather than going wilder: teammates-trade-shifts (=innovator #4), calendar/channel delivery (=innovator #2), schedule-first-ask-later (=innovator #1/#7), and rival-export-untangle (=innovator #3 import) all reappear. Same mechanisms, new phrasing, so novelty (S1) and diversity (S4) both collapse on that cell.

[substance] Within b2b innovator, ~5 of 8 ideas fold into a single mechanism family ('remove setup friction to reach the first finished week': #1 poll-draft, #3 import-rota, #7 stalled-team-draft, #8 kickoff-link, plus #2 channel-delivery sharing the adoption-without-login idea with #4). Eight distinct pitches, roughly two real mechanism families.

[substance] Cafe innovator leans on the standard cafe-revenue playbook: rent idle ovens, wholesale loaves, office coffee delivery, brew-coaching class, tasting-space rental, grab-and-go fridge are all obvious moves. Well-executed but low novelty (S1); only the morning-token upsell and afternoon-desk subscription are mildly fresh.

[substance] Vivid examples mask under-specified mechanisms (S2 inflation). 'Pay out saved hours as a coffee round funded from the subscription' (b2b wild_card #3), 'free hours expire Sunday' (#8), and 'stream the quiet room as paid background' (cafe wild_card #5) wrap a concrete sentence around a slogan: how saved hours are measured, how the payout economics work, and how streaming an empty room yields afternoon revenue are all hand-waved.

[substance] The two 'banked/expiring saved hours' ideas (b2b wild_card #3, #8) attack retention/loyalty in general, not the stated root cause of first-60-day activation failure, weakening relevance (S3).

[substance] Several WILD-tagged cafe wild_card ideas (streaming the room, phone-lockbox) are novel but thin on actual afternoon revenue and feasibility, so relevance to 'grow afternoon revenue without cannibalising the morning rush' is weaker than the novelty suggests.

[compliance] Business-jargon leaks break the coffee-talk frame: 'standing B2B order' / 'B2B order' (cafe innovator #2), 'tap-to-pay self-checkout', 'billable hours', 'recurring revenue', and 'CSV export' (b2b sets).

[compliance] The b2b sets read as dense pitch-copy rather than self-contained coffee-talk, packing terms like admin, conflict-free, draft, CSV and onboarding into the 2-3 sentence window, which lowers C1/C3 relative to the breezier cafe sets.

[substance] wild_card does not reliably out-novel innovator: the idle-barista paid brewing class appears in BOTH cafe sets (innovator #6, wild_card #7), undercutting the premise that the wild persona generates more distinct ideas.

[substance] Heavy cross-persona duplication in the SaaS topic: peer-to-peer shift swaps (innovator #4, wild_card #2), schedule-lands-in-the-channel/calendar-you-already-use (innovator #2, wild_card #4), and schedule-first-ask-permission-later (innovator #7, wild_card #7) all recur, so wild_card mostly re-skins innovator's mechanisms rather than reaching new ones.

[substance] Several cafe/innovator ideas are standard cafe-revenue playbook with low novelty despite polished delivery: office delivery round (#3), room-rental-for-tastings (#5), wholesale loaves to the bistro (#2), and barista coaching (#6) are well-known moves; their S1 sits at 2-3 even though mechanism specificity is high.

[substance] Many afternoon-revenue ideas sidestep the stated 'without cannibalising the morning rush' tension rather than attacking it: rent-the-ovens (#1), wholesale loaves (#2), and parcel-pickup (wild_card #8) just add afternoon revenue without engaging the constraint, so their S3 relevance is lower than the morning-token (#4) and afternoon-only-subscription (#7) ideas that explicitly protect the rush.

[substance] Low tag spread in the wild_card sets weakens batch diversity: SaaS/wild_card is 6 WILD / 2 BOLD / 0 SAFE and cafe/wild_card is 5 WILD / 2 BOLD / 1 SAFE, so the sets cluster on one altitude despite the mechanisms themselves being individually distinct.

[compliance] Minor jargon leakage in the SaaS sets ('CSV export', 'B2B', 'fantasy-sports draft', 'use-it-or-lose-it') nudges C3 slightly below the cafe sets, though it stays well within coffee-talk range overall.
